content:
Hey everyone,

AutoCorres2 is an Isabelle framework for verifying C code. Roughly, if Aeneas goes from Rust to Lean, then AutoCorres2 goes from C to Isabelle. It has been used to verify the seL4 microkernel in the past (v1, anyway) and is used by big players in industry.
Furthermore, the bulk of it can be recast as a (partially evaluated) denotational semantics from C AST into a certain SpecM monad if you simply skip the SIMPL IR (I don't see a reason to keep it).
Reason enough for me to see how we could port it to Lean and use mvcgen to reason about SpecM programs. You can find the result of a couple of days of vibe coding at https://github.com/sgraf812/LeanCorres.
I'd say that mvcgen works for this use case, but of course much more work needs to be done to turn this PoC into a proper tool. OTOH

  1. One would need to write the proper C to Clight AST frontend
  2. There needs to be what AutoCorres2 calls the "unified memory model"; a heap typing discipline maintained in a separation logic. (Aside: mvcgen will get support for VC generation into separation logics in Q2, but it's not there yet.)

Anyway, wanted to post these findings before they bitrot in my repo. This might be interesting to pursue for industry players.

1. One would need to write the proper C to Clight AST frontend

Have you considered targeting one of the CompCert IRs?
With https://peregrine-project.github.io/ we're providing a shared middle-end, which already includes a lean front-end, it would be great to add more such connections across provers.

I instructed Claude to target CompCert's Clight IR as the AST on which the denotational semantics into SpecM is defined. So what's missing is tooling integration for the C->Clight translation, perhaps implemented by a Lean port of clightgen. But so far, it's just a subset of Clight; judging by this diagram, it's quite possible that we should rather target Cminor for the den sem. I'm not sure if code extraction is a goal here; it doesn't seem to be for AutoCorres.

extraction is likely useful for other projects too. Once the infrastructure is in place, people will likely find a use for it.
RefinedC with iris-lean could also be an future project to integrate with.

Sebastian Graf said:

  1. (Aside: mvcgen will get support for VC generation into separation logics in Q2, but it's not there yet.)

This sounds very intriguing. Can you already say something more about what the plans for separation logic and mvcgen are?
bedrock2 could be another inspiration. It's been used for production code.

This sounds very intriguing. Can you already say something more about what the plans for separation logic and mvcgen are?

The plan is to open up the meta theory such that there can be WP instances that relate a monad m to a separation logic l (which must still be a CompleteLattice). With the current WP formulation that relates m to a fixed ps : PostShape that's impossible. With the new meta theory, it is possible to translate a program in m and a post condition on m in said separation logic into VCs in said separation logic using mvcgen.

extraction is likely useful for other projects too. Once the infrastructure is in place, people will likely find a use for it.

It is, but it's not the goal for AutoCorres I think. AutoCorres instead takes production C code and produces Isabelle code that models the semantics of the production C code (this translation is part of the TCB) in order to prove properties about the model.
There is no extraction step because the C code is pre-existing.

Extraction facilities and bedrock2 in Lean are independently worthwhile, but as I see it, it's out of scope for what non-PoC LeanCorres aims at.
